hypothesis_text: High level of NFKB, a transcription factor mediating inflammation, before vaccination is associated with poor response to Hepatitis B vaccine
population: healthy humans receiving hepatitis B vaccination

predictor.biological_factor: Baseline NF-kB pathway activity / inflammatory transcriptional tone
possible_measurements: pre-vaccination whole blood or PBMC expression of NF-kB subunit genes (NFKB1, NFKB2, RELA, RELB, REL)
NF-kB target gene signature score (e.g., hallmark TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB) at baseline
NF-kB inhibitor/regulator gene expression (NFKBIA, NFKBIE, TNFAIP3)
phospho-p65 or nuclear NF-kB by flow cytometry/CyTOF at baseline
baseline serum inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-6, IL-1B, CXCL8) as NF-kB activity proxy

outcome.name: Hepatitis B vaccine response (anti-HBs antibody)
possible_measurements: fold change in anti-HBs from baseline to post-vaccination
HBsAg-specific B cell or T cell responses by ELISPOT/flow cytometry

required_data: pre-vaccination transcriptomic (or protein/phospho) measurement permitting NF-kB pathway quantification
post-vaccination anti-HBs antibody titer or defined responder status
subject-level linkage between baseline molecular data and antibody outcome

scientific_criteria.description: Participants received a hepatitis B vaccine (any licensed formulation, primary series or booster).
Biological samples were collected before the vaccine dose (baseline/day 0).
Study contains an assay from which NF-kB pathway activity can be quantified at baseline (transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq, phospho-flow/CyTOF, or inflammatory protein panel).
Post-vaccination hepatitis B vaccine response was measured, e.g., anti-HBs titer, seroconversion, or responder/non-responder classification.
At least one outcome timepoint occurs after vaccination, allowing assessment of response.
Baseline molecular measurements and post-vaccination antibody outcomes can be linked within the same participants via subject identifiers.
Study includes enough vaccinated participants with both measurements to observe variation in vaccine response (roughly 10 or more).

operational_criteria.description: Raw or processed assay data files are available for download from ImmPort or a linked repository (e.g., GEO/SRA).
Subject-level metadata with timepoints, treatment arm, and sample-to-subject mapping are present.
Anti-HBs titer or responder status values are present in the study's lab test or assay result tables, not only in the publication text.

primary_statistical_test.example_model: log10_antiHBs_peak ~ baseline_NFkB_score + age + sex + baseline_antiHBs + batch

recommended_analysis.predictor: Baseline (day 0) NF-kB target gene signature score computed from whole blood/PBMC expression (or mean z-score of NFKB1, NFKB2, RELA, RELB, REL, NFKBIA)
recommended_analysis.outcome: Peak post-vaccination anti-HBs titer (log10 mIU/mL) or binary responder status (>=10 mIU/mL)
recommended_analysis.model: log10_antiHBs_peak ~ baseline_NFkB_score + age + sex + baseline_antiHBs + batch
